repair_info.name: Temperature High Issue
repair_info.image_alt_text: iPhone Xs Max Temperature High Issue

data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX comes with a special thermal compound in the back area of the phone which helps to omit heat faster and more efficiently than the previous iPhones. It may make your iPhone seem a lot hotter than the previous iPhones. However, that doesn’t make the iPhone XS MAX so warm that the users find it difficult to hold it down with their hands. This is a clear indication of overheating in the iPhone XS MAX. Some similar cases of overheating include.

  • Phone gets way too hot while charging and takes a long time to be fully charged
  • Phone gets hot and the battery drains drastically.
  • You might see a notification that will say “Temperature high”
  • The iPhone gets warm on standby mode for no apparent reasons whatsoever.

(Note: if your phone gets too hot while transferring data for the first time from a previous iPhone, chances are it’s a one-time issue and will not happen again.)

These are some of the most discussed problems in Apple’s user threads and community. However, there are some DIY (Do it Yourself) fixes that you may try which may help you to resolve your overheating issues.

  • Disable background app refresh.
  • Disable background app refresh from here: Settings > General > Background App Refresh
  • Turn off Bluetooth / Location services to reduce processes running in the background
  • Most of the users have reported they get the heating issue in the latest iOS version, In that case,
  • try updating your iOS to later versions to check if it works for your phone.

If none of the fixes above work for you, you might need to get it looked at by professional technicians who specialize in resolving iPhone XS MAX heating issues. repair_info.name: Proximity Sensor Replacement
repair_info.image_alt_text: iPhone Xs Max Proximity Sensor Replacement

data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX is a smartphone that has a lot of ambient sensors such as an accelerometer, a gyroscopic sensor, and a proximity sensor. The proximity sensor is probably the most used in your iPhone. This sensor is used for turning your phone’s screen off when it is placed near your face during a phone call. So that it may conserve battery or avoid unnecessary touch inputs by your face when talking. It may also be used for features like “Raise and Wake” and other minimal yet handy features.

However, you may face problems in the proximity sensor of your iPhone XS MAX over time. Some issues of the iPhone XS MAX proximity sensor reported by users of the iPhone XS Max in the users' community are:

  • The proximity sensor is not working/ too sensitive. And turning the phone screen on and off during calls.
  • The phone display doesn’t turn off during a phone call
  • The phone display doesn’t turn on automatically as it should after the phone call ends.

These are the most common issues found in the iPhone XS MAX proximity sensor. There are some DIY (Do it yourself) fixes you may try which may solve issues regarding your proximity sensor if they are very minor. Apple recommends:

  • Try removing your screen protector which may block the proximity sensors proper working.
  • Restart your iPhone
  • Update your iOS.

If you have already tried the above-mentioned fixes and none of the fixes work for you, you might need to get your phone checked by a professional technician. data.title: Liquid Damage
data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX is a standard IP68 rated, dust and water-resistant phone. This means it can resist dust and water coming in up to a certain level. However, it is not completely immune to water getting inside the iPhone and damaging it. Apple has introduced a new technology called LCI. LCI is an abbreviation for liquid contact indicator. It is located in the sim tray region. Now you can see the LCI when you remove the sim tray, buy putting the ejector pin into the sim tray ejection hole. Once you have removed the sim tray, you should see a white/red portion inside the sim tray region. That is your LCI on the iPhone. If the LCI is completely white or silver then it is okay. The phone hasn’t contacted any water. However, if your LCI turns red you can safely assume that it has been in touch with water and has taken in some water damage.

If you have dropped your phone in the water here are some basic things you should do:

  • Rinse your phone with a lens cloth or a microfiber cloth
  • You may gently tap the phone with the charger hole against your hand. It may drip the water out if it has gotten in there.
  • NEVER CHARGE YOUR PHONE UNTIL YOU HAVE MADE SURE IT IS COMPLETELY DRY
  • If anything spills on your phone other than water (like oil etc.) just rinse the place with a lint-free cloth.
  • If water has gotten into your phone, it may damage your Battery, Charging port, or give you muffled speakers.

The new iPhone XS MAX offers its users better optimization and balance in software than the previous iPhone models. This problem happens mainly/most of the time because of a software issue that happens due to an unclean or interrupted update.

This Stuck on Apple logo issue might happen in other instances too. Possible reasons might be:

  • The iPhone has taken in some physical damage. (Dropping from hand)
  • Update was disrupted due to Wi-Fi disturbance/metered connection or cellular data loss.
  • A third-party app may have access to vital permissions that can disrupt iPhones' productivity.
  • It is rare; however, your phone might be facing a hardware issue. Sometimes faulty hardware prevents the phone from booting up.

These issues however can be resolved if it is just a bug or a glitch in the iOS software. You may try the following steps and see if it works for you.

  • Force Restart your iPhone XS MAX

(Press volume up (+) and then quickly press volume down (-) button and hold the iPhone XS MAX power button as long as the apple logo appears again)

  • Update your iOS Software.

(If, while in the progress of updating your software, the progress bar under the Apple logo has not moved for an hour, you may connect your iPhone to a PC and select “Update” when prompted)

  • Remove all third-party apps from your phone. Install Apps only from the Apple App store

Turn off the auto-update of your iOS apps to prevent further interruptions. BUT BE SURE TO UPDATE THEM IN REGULAR BASIS MANUALLY.

If none of the fixes above work, for you. You might have an issue that needs the touch of a professional iPhone technician.   • Restarting Your Phone

data.description:
The new iPhone XS MAX offers one of the best displays consisting of a Liquid Retina IPS LCD display and a significantly high DPI. It has also ensured maximum safety for its users by putting gorilla glass in both back and front. However, not all damage in display comes from dropping the device from the hands and shattering it. The No light on Display issue of the iPhone XS MAX is where the user can’t see what’s happening on the phone. The phone runs okay. The phone vibrates and the user can hear the notification sounds and other inputs. But the problem is they can not see any of it because the phone display is just plain black. But the phone will respond or might even have incoming calls.

The key symptoms of the “No light on Display” issues are:

The Phone display boots up with an Apple logo but doesn’t get past the black screen (iPhone 6 – 8Plus)

The phone has calls, notifications but doesn’t show anything on display

iPhone can charge (you can hear the sound that the phone makes while charging) but won’t show anything on the display.

This “No light on display” is usually an internal issue with the LCD connector. However, Apple recommends some processes to practice on your phone to make sure the black screen is not a software glitch.

Force Restart your iPhone.

(Press the volume up (+) and volume down (-) and then press and hold the power button until the Apple logo appears on the screen)

Connect the lightning cable, charge it for 10 minutes. Then try force restarting the iPhone.

UNCONVENTIONAL: But press the screen into the phone so it may reconnect any dislodged LCD connector. This fix is not recommended however it resolved a lot of the user's Black Display issue. It might be risky for any layman person.

The phone throttles heavily, shuts off unexpectedly at 20–30% remaining, and requires charging multiple times a day. Battery replacement is essential for any owner continuing to use this phone. Cracked Super Retina OLED screen

The 6.5-inch OLED panel cracks and develops the permanent symptoms of OLED damage — green or pink lines, dead pixel columns, and complete touch failure in damaged zones. Full assembly replacement is the only solution. [→ iPhone Xs Max screen replacement]

Face ID failure — the most common non-battery fault

Face ID failure is disproportionately common on the Xs Max versus older Touch ID iPhones. TrueDepth sensor failure from drops, moisture reaching the sensor cluster, and Face ID pairing broken by prior screen repairs are all causes. iFixit BD diagnoses Face ID independently from screen damage and preserves pairing during every screen replacement. [→ iPhone Xs Max Face ID repair]

Dual camera — telephoto blur or Portrait Mode depth failure

The iPhone Xs Max's dual camera system powers Portrait Mode. Telephoto lens failure from a drop, OIS wear, and flex cable damage degrade Portrait Mode and zoom quality. [→ iPhone Xs Max camera repair]

Lightning port worn after 7 years of daily use

Seven years of daily cable connections wear the Lightning port pins down to the point where cables fall out or charging fails entirely. Port cleaning and flex cable replacement are both services we offer. [→ iPhone Xs Max charging issues]
